caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2537 of 2009
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate (Mr. Obaidur Rahman Mustafa, Advocate with him) instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Chittagong Zilla Parishad represented by its Chief Executive Officer, Chittagong Zilla Parishad, and Chittagong ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Nurul Haque and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel for the petitioner has mainly argued to the effect that the lower appellate court and the High Court Division have committed great error in not considering at all the fact that Abdul Latif was a ejaradar for a limited period under the Chittagong Zilla Parishad, that though the relevant khatian-the exhibit-1 and the exhibit-A clearly showed that Nabid Ali was a mere "dakhalkar" under Abdul Latif and Abdul Latif was a ejaradar under Chittagong Zilla Parishad for a period of 5 years only but both the High Court Division and the lower appellate court have failed to take into consideration these documentary evidence at all and also to comprehend the same and thus have failed to come to a right decision. Drawing our attention to exhibit-A the learned Counsel for the petitioner has argued that this exhibit-A proves clearly that Chittagong District Board was the owner of the suit land and under this landlord Abdul Latif was a mere ejaradar for a period of five years only from 1926-1931 and in the circumstances Abdul Latif had no right to settle the suit land to Nabid Ali. The learned Counsel has contended that this exhibit-A along with exhibit-1 proves also the case of the contesting defendants that Nabid Ali was a mere "dakhalkar" under Abdul Latif. The learned Counsel has contended also that long before promulgation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the ejara right of Abdul Latif ceased to exist and as such the Chittagong Zilla Parishad took back the khas possession of the suit land and the suit land remained in the khas possession of the defendant No. 1 and the defendant No. 1 subsequently leased out the suit land to defendant No. 2 lawfully. The learned Counsel has argued to the effect also that there are sufficient evidence on record-both oral and documentary which proved that Chittagong Zilla Parishad was in possession of the suit land along with other lands and has been possessing those lands by giving temporary lease to different persons; but the lower appellate court and also the High Court Division have failed to appreciate these evidence on record and consequently arrived at a wrong decision which cannot be sustained in law.
